activity_context.topic_title: Asymptotes of Hyperbolas Centered at the Origin

feedback.problem:
The asymptotes of the hyperbola $4{y}^{2}-9{x}^{2}=36$ are$\,\,y=\pm $
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The standard equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

For a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin, the equations of the asymptotes are

$$
y=\pm \frac{a}{b}x.
$$

To rewrite the given equation in standard form, we divide both sides of the equation by $36$ and then simplify, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{y}^{2}-9{x}^{2} & =36 \\ \frac{4{y}^{2}}{36}-\frac{9{x}^{2}}{36} & =\frac{36}{36} \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{9}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have $a=\sqrt{9}=3$ and $b=\sqrt{4}=2.$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\pm \frac{3}{2}x.\end{aligned}
$$
